items.summary: Legal disposition: blocked for public beta or full launch; keep SearchWoot private. Woot documentation confirms API access but not commercial/public redistribution, storage, historical derivatives, display, alerts, affiliate, advertising, attribution, freshness, correction, or takedown rights. Current public terms point against the proposed use. Human counsel is required before any rights outreach, data-use expansion, affiliate use, advertising, or public exposure. Fleet evidence also shows 35 compliance passes, 20 failures, 6 unknowns; security and operations sweeps have no results; accuracy/freshness, measurement/attribution, and owner gates remain blocked. Ordinary reversible growth may continue only where it does not add data collection, rights exposure, regulated claims, or new monetization.

Candidate-plan review: retain the capacity gate and reject new site-factory, CRO, telemetry, duplicate-control-plane, and production admissions this cycle. The only supported next action is completion or justified closure of the existing saveusfarms.com repair case by 2026-10-01T09:00Z, followed by at most the already-canonical allthingsmasonic.com CTA work after capacity release. Preserve affiliate disclosure, destination integrity, accessibility, rollback, and measurement boundaries; do not claim revenue, ROI, conversion lift, or causality. The available Amazon evidence is limited to 2026-09-21 aggregate commission of $4.92 under tracking_id=other and is not site-attributable.

Launch-readiness tracking progress: 0 of 4 SearchWoot legal tasks are closed; all remain open. Existing evidence is partial for data flow and consent/analytics, while source rights are blocked. Do not mark tasks complete based on repository files alone. Next evidence action: attach one dated read-only bundle containing the authoritative source-rights record, field-level data-flow/retention table, deployed consent and GA4 configuration evidence, and log/vendor/incident inventory; then obtain human-counsel review for rights, privacy, and jurisdictional questions.
